data.cultural_impact: Ganesh is one of the most widely worshipped deities in the Hindu pantheon. He is intricately linked to Indian culture, traditions, and festivities, particularly in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Karnataka. The annual festival of Ganesh Chaturthi, celebrated in September, is a grand affair marked by the installation of magnificent idols, processions, and immersion in water bodies. Ganesh's story is an essential component of the Indian epic Mahabharata and is also recounted in various Puranas and Itihasas. The depiction of Ganesh with his elephant head, large ears, and four arms holding symbols of wisdom, prosperity, auspiciousness, and protection, is ubiquitous and believed to bring good fortune and longevity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Ganesh is considered the symbol of wisdom, intelligence, and the removal of obstacles. He is also known as Vighnaharta or the God of obstacles due to his power to destroy every obstacle that hinders the progress of his devotees in their spiritual journey. He is believed to bestow knowledge and wisdom upon his devotees. Ganesh is the logistical coordinator and facilitator for Gods and the god of wisdom, learning, and education. He is often depicted as the one who grants boons and unknown powers and is hence invoked before starting any new venture. His elephant head symbolizes the all-knowing, all-seeing power of the divine consciousness, and his large ears symbolize his ability to listen and understand the prayers of his devotees.

name_in_real_life.story: Priya Ganes, a teacher in Bangalore, India, shares that their name Ganes meaning "Lord of Beginnings" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ganesh, the elephant-headed god, symbolizes the removal of obstacles and the embodiment of wisdom and new beginnings. His large ears signify listening attentively, while his broken tusk represents the ability to learn from past mistakes.

seo.title: Ganes - Hinduism God of Wisdom and Remover of Obstacles
seo.meta_description: Ganes is a popular Hinduism name for a god of wisdom, prosperity, and good fortune. Known as the remover of obstacles, he is revered for his intelligence, strength, and benevolence.
seo.description_paragraph: Ganes is one of the most widely revered deities in the Hindu pantheon. Originally known as Ganesha, he is the god of wisdom, knowledge, and learning, and is also considered a patron of arts and sciences. In Hindu mythology, Ganes is depicted as having an elephant head and a human body, and he is often shown holding a goad, a noose, and a bowl full of rice. He is also the god of fertility, and is believed to bring good fortune and prosperity. Ganes is often invoked at the beginning of new ventures and projects, as he is believed to remove obstacles and pave the way for success. He is also known as the god of wisdom and knowledge, and is believed to bestow wisdom and intelligence upon those who seek his blessings. Ganes is a beloved deity in Hinduism, and is revered by millions around the world.
